cases.explain: Мальчик is a predicate noun describing the subject, so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Стало быть, показал он этот спектакль и надушил здесь серый не для ___, а для демонстрации.
cases.explain: The preposition для (for) always governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: И вы начинаете относиться к самому себе как к третьему ___.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Я имел подлость убить сегодня эту ___.
cases.explain: Чайку is the direct object of the transitive verb убить (to kill), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: С такой ___, с таким чудесным голосом.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) describing accompanying qualities governs the instrumental case.
The preposition в (in) denoting location/topic governs the prepositional case here.

reading.ru: Ирина Матушка, нельзя так обращаться с молодым самолюбием.
reading.question: What does the speaker tell Irina about how she treated the young man?
options: She should not have treated his pride so harshly
She should praise his talent more often
She should let him direct a real theater
reading.correct: She should not have treated his pride so harshly
reading.explain: The line says one must not treat a young man's pride (self-love) that way.

reading.ru: Стало быть, показал он этот спектакль и надушил здесь серый не для шутки, а для демонстрации.
reading.question: According to this line, why did Konstantin stage his play with such theatrical effects (like sulfur smoke)?
options: To demonstrate his new artistic ideas, not as a joke
reading.correct: To demonstrate his new artistic ideas, not as a joke
reading.explain: The speaker concludes the smoke and staging were 'for demonstration,' not for a joke.

reading.ru: Просто капризный самолюбивый мальчик.
reading.question: How does Irina (Arkadina) describe her son in this line?
reading.correct: A capricious, vain boy
reading.explain: She calls him 'просто капризный самолюбивый мальчик' — simply a capricious, vain boy.

reading.ru: Никто не имеет основания отделять дух от материи, так как, быть может, самый дух есть совокупность материальных атомов.
reading.question: What philosophical idea from Konstantin's play is being quoted here?
options: That spirit and matter cannot be separated, since spirit may be a collection of material atoms
That nature is more important than art
That death is the only truth
reading.correct: That spirit and matter cannot be separated, since spirit may be a collection of material atoms
reading.explain: The line states no one has grounds to separate spirit from matter, since spirit may itself be a collection of material atoms.

reading.ru: Жен-премьером и кумиром тогда всех шести усадьб был вот, рекомендую, доктор Евгений Сергеевич Романов.
reading.question: Who is identified as the former idol and heartthrob of the six estates years ago?
reading.correct: Doctor Evgeny Sergeyevich (Dorn)
reading.explain: The text names 'доктор Евгений Сергеевич' as the leading man and idol of all six estates at that time.

reading.ru: С такой наружностью, с таким чудесным голосом Нельзя грешно сидеть в деревне Вы должны поступить на сцену У вас должен быть талант Ой, это моя мечта Но она никогда не осуществится Кто знает Позвольте представить Тригорин Борис Алексеевич.
reading.question: Who is being introduced to Nina in this passage?
reading.correct: The writer Trigorin
reading.explain: The passage ends with the introduction: 'Позвольте представить Тригорин Борис Алексеевич.'

reading.ru: Он хоть и знаменитый, но очень простой человек.
reading.question: How does Nina describe Trigorin despite his fame?
options: As a very simple, unpretentious man
reading.correct: As a very simple, unpretentious man
reading.explain: She says though he is famous, he is 'очень простой человек' — a very simple person.

reading.ru: Для меня нет большего наслаждения, чем сидеть под вечер на берегу и смотреть на поплавок.
reading.question: What does Trigorin say gives him the greatest pleasure?
options: Sitting by the shore in the evening watching a fishing float
reading.correct: Sitting by the shore in the evening watching a fishing float
reading.explain: Trigorin says there is no greater pleasure for him than sitting by the shore in the evening watching the float.

reading.ru: Говорят, ее покойная мать оставила все свое огромное состояние своему мужу.
reading.question: What is said about Masha's late mother?
options: She left her whole large fortune to her husband
She died of illness in the city
reading.correct: She left her whole large fortune to her husband
reading.explain: The text says her late mother left her entire large fortune to her husband.

reading.ru: Когда эта девочка говорила об одиночестве.
reading.question: What topic in Nina's performance moved Sorin, according to this line?
options: When the girl spoke about loneliness
reading.correct: When the girl spoke about loneliness
reading.explain: Sorin recalls being moved 'когда эта девочка говорила об одиночестве' — when the girl spoke of loneliness.

reading.ru: Константин Гаврилович, мне ваша пьеса чрезвычайно понравилась.
reading.question: What does Nina tell Konstantin about his play?
options: That she liked it very much
That she did not understand any of it
reading.correct: That she liked it very much
reading.explain: Nina tells him, 'мне ваша пьеса чрезвычайно понравилась' — she liked his play very much.

reading.ru: Так и следовало, потому что художественное произведение непременно должно выражать какую-нибудь большую мысль.
reading.question: According to Dorn, what must a work of art necessarily express?
reading.correct: Some great idea
reading.explain: Dorn says a work of art must necessarily express some great idea ('большую мысль').

reading.ru: Иначе, если вы пойдете по этой живописной дороге без определенной цели, вы заблудитесь, и ваш талант погубит вас.
reading.question: What warning does Dorn give Konstantin about following an undefined path?
options: That he will lose his way and his talent will destroy him
That he should stop writing altogether
That he should marry Nina soon
That he should leave the estate
reading.correct: That he will lose his way and his talent will destroy him
reading.explain: Dorn warns that without a definite goal, Konstantin 'заблудится, и ваш талант погубит вас' — will lose his way and his talent will ruin him.

reading.ru: Мне необходимо ее видеть.
reading.question: What does Konstantin desperately want after learning Nina left?
options: He needs to talk to his mother
He needs to finish his play
reading.correct: He needs to see her
reading.explain: He repeats 'Мне необходимо ее видеть' — I need to see her.

reading.ru: Я не люблю своего отца, но к вам почему-то лежит мое сердце.
reading.question: What does Masha say about her feelings toward Dorn compared to her father?
options: She does not love her father, but her heart is drawn to Dorn
She loves her father more than anyone
She hates both her father and Dorn
She wants to move away from both
reading.correct: She does not love her father, but her heart is drawn to Dorn
reading.explain: Masha says she doesn't love her own father, but her heart is somehow drawn to Dorn.

reading.ru: Я люблю Константина.
reading.question: Who does Masha confess she loves?
reading.correct: Konstantin
reading.explain: Masha says plainly 'Я люблю Константина' — I love Konstantin.

reading.ru: Вам 22 года.
reading.question: What age difference is being pointed out in this exchange?
options: The speaker is almost twice as old as the listener, who is 22
The listener is older than the speaker
reading.correct: The speaker is almost twice as old as the listener, who is 22
reading.explain: The line states 'Вам 22 года. Я почти вдвое вас старше' — you are 22, I am almost twice your age.

reading.ru: Итак, когда женщина избрала писателя, которого она желает заполонить, она осаждает его посредством комплиментов, любезности и угождений.
reading.question: According to this passage, how does a woman who wants to captivate a writer act?
options: She besieges him with compliments, courtesies, and favors
reading.correct: She besieges him with compliments, courtesies, and favors
reading.explain: The text says she 'осаждает его посредством комплиментов, любезности и угождений' — besieges him with compliments and favors.

reading.ru: Отец и мачеха уехали в Тверь, и мы теперь свободны целых три дня.
reading.question: What happened that gave the speaker three days of freedom?
options: Her father and stepmother left for Tver
reading.correct: Her father and stepmother left for Tver
reading.explain: The line says the father and stepmother went to Tver, leaving them free for three whole days.

reading.ru: Мне кажется, ему хорошо было бы сейчас поехать куда-нибудь на воды.
reading.question: What does the doctor suggest Sorin should do for his health?
options: Go somewhere to take the waters (a health spa)
reading.correct: Go somewhere to take the waters (a health spa)
reading.explain: The line suggests it would be good for Sorin to go somewhere to 'take the waters' now.

reading.ru: И вы начинаете относиться к самому себе как к третьему лицу.
reading.question: What effect of smoking and drinking is described here?
options: You start relating to yourself as if you were a third person
reading.correct: You start relating to yourself as if you were a third person
reading.explain: The text says after smoking or drinking, 'вы начинаете относиться к самому себе как к третьему лицу' — you start treating yourself as a third person.

reading.ru: Я прослужил по судебному ведомству 28 лет.
reading.question: How many years did the speaker serve in the judicial department?
reading.correct: 28 years
reading.explain: The speaker states, 'Я прослужил по судебному ведомству 28 лет.'

reading.ru: В таком случае я немедленно уезжаю в Москву.
reading.question: What does Irina Nikolaevna (Arkadina) threaten to do if she cannot get horses?
options: Fire the estate manager on the spot
reading.correct: Leave immediately for Moscow
reading.explain: She declares, 'В таком случае я немедленно уезжаю в Москву' — in that case I am leaving for Moscow immediately.

reading.ru: Отказать Ирине Николаевне, знаменитой артистке.
reading.question: Who is being refused horses in this complaint?
reading.correct: Irina Nikolaevna, the famous actress
reading.explain: The line complains about refusing horses to 'Ирине Николаевне, знаменитой артистке' — Irina Nikolaevna, the famous actress.

reading.ru: Я сейчас же пойду и поговорю с ним.
reading.question: What does the speaker decide to do to resolve the horse dispute?
options: Go and talk to him (the manager) right away
Call for new horses to be bought
reading.correct: Go and talk to him (the manager) right away
reading.explain: The speaker says, 'Я сейчас же пойду и поговорю с ним' — I will go and talk to him right now.
